slot.brief: Definite integral of odd function over symmetric interval, or even-function split; require recognition step plus a standard result.

verdicts.working: The odd term $x^3$ integrates to $0$ on $[-1,1]$. The remaining integral is $[\arctan x]_{-1}^{1}=\pi/2$.

working:
$x^3$ is odd, so its integral over $[-1,1]$ is $0$.\n$\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{dx}{1+x^2}=2\int_0^1\frac{dx}{1+x^2}=2[\arctan x]_0^1=\frac{\pi}{2}$.

solution:
Since $x^3$ is odd, $[?]$ its integral over $[-1,1]$ is zero. Also,
$$\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{dx}{1+x^2}=[\arctan x]_{-1}^{1}=\frac{\pi}{4}-\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}.$$
Hence the value is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
